name: WA-02
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Rick Larsen running with large financial advantage
model.rationale: Larsen is a well-funded incumbent in a D+12 district, while Feller has raised less than $9,000 and shows no outside support. Markets and fundamentals both point to an easy Larsen win, so the forecast stays near the baseline with only a slight trim for the favorable Republican environment.
model.watch: A late surge of outside spending against Larsen or an unusually strong national Republican wave could narrow the margin, though not enough to threaten the seat.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview: Rick Larsen, a long-serving Democratic incumbent, seeks another term in a northwestern Washington district that leans Democratic by about twelve points. He has raised more than two million dollars and holds over $650,000 on hand, while Republican challenger Edwin Feller has raised under nine thousand dollars with no outside backing. Prediction markets give Larsen roughly a 96% chance of winning. No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the outlook rests on the district's lean, the incumbency advantage, and the lopsided financial picture. The national environment may be somewhat favorable to Republicans, which could shave a few points off Larsen's margin, but nothing in the evidence suggests a competitive race. Larsen remains a heavy favorite for reelection.
